question.problem: Use trial and error to find the solutions, if any, to the congruence $4x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,6).$
question.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=6$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3,4,5$ into the equation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot 0 & ≡0≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 1 & ≡4≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 2 & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & ✓ \\ 4\cdot 3 & ≡0≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 4 & ≡4≢2 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & \times  \\ 4\cdot 5 & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) &  & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the solutions are $x≡2,5$ only $(\text{mod}\,6).$
